bg.purpose: The page itself — the stock everything is printed on. Painted by `body` in semantic.css; every surface role is a step away from it.

bg-raised.purpose: The separated sheet — cards, table rows, alerts. One ladder step off the page (darker than it in Solace light; which way the ladder travels is a per-theme decision). It carries no border of its own: the drawn shade is what says raised.

bg-overlay.purpose: The far end of the ladder: dialogs, sheets, menus, select panels, an interactive card under hover.

bg-input.purpose: tone-0, the ramp's anchor and every knockout. In Solace it equals surface-0 in both schemes — one origin, two axes — so a writing field sits flush with the page and is bounded by its stroke, not its fill. It is a different token from bg-raised, and since this revision a different value.

bg-emphasis.purpose: The deepest ramp step (tone-11) and the emphasis material: strong borders and the primary button fill are one and the same ink. Body text is no longer part of that identity — fg moved to tone-10 in this revision so a paragraph does not read at primary-button pressure.

fg-muted.purpose: Secondary type only. The ramp's middle is never used for a stroke.

border.purpose: Pressure two: the stroke that bounds a control. 3.05:1 on the stock.

border-muted.purpose: Fused-strip frames, table footers, and every disabled border (always dashed).

border-subtle.purpose: Pressure three, added in this revision: a divider inside a surface. Its only consumer in the shipped set is the table row rule — Separator and the dropdown/select menu rules still draw at border-muted. 1.71:1 on raised paper, correct for a seam and insufficient for anything load-bearing.

border-strong.purpose: Pressure one: a boundary that outranks the page — a table header rule, a menu panel frame, a badge.

accent-solid.purpose: The single vivid voice. Hover and open-state edges, the focus outline, the caret, link text. Never a resting fill, never decoration.

accent-bg.purpose: Behind the currently navigated menu or select row, always with the 2px inset leading rule and ink type.

accent-bg-subtle.purpose: The lens plate under the current navigation cell or tab. Measures 1.12:1 light and 1.10:1 dark — a recorded gap, not a target.

danger-solid.purpose: Destructive actions, invalid fields, destructive menu rows.

warning-solid.purpose: Caution, and the only signal knocked out in ink. 1.76:1 on paper — may fill a shape, must never be the only thing drawing a boundary.

warning-fg.purpose: The rule color Alert's warning variant borrows, because the ochre solid cannot hold a hairline on paper.

info-alt-solid.purpose: A second information voice when two must be distinguished.

display.purpose: 20px/700. Page-level headings on documentation and Storybook surfaces. No registry component uses it.

headline.purpose: 18px/600 on 28px literal leading. Dialog and Sheet titles only — the one place a component raises its voice.

title.purpose: Inherited size at 600 and leading-tight; Card sets no size on its root. Card titles and in-component headings — weight does the work. leading-none clipped 1.13px of Latin descenders and was retired.

body.purpose: 14px/1.55. The interface voice: labels, menu rows, table cells and headers (600), input text, default and large buttons, tabs, navigation, pagination. 28 of the 36 explicit size utilities in the component sources.

label.purpose: 12px/1.45. Badges, the small button size, tooltips, menu group labels and shortcuts. The CJK floor — no script goes below it. Six of the 36.

mono.purpose: 12px/1.45 monospace. Code badges and inline code only.

shadows.name: offset
shadows.purpose: Surface shade. A raised card, a table with `shadow`. Static. Now the load-bearing signal that a surface is raised, since surfaces dropped their borders.

shadows.name: offset-overlay
shadows.purpose: Overlay shade. Dialogs, sheets, menus, select panels, a card at `overlay` elevation. Darker grey for a higher layer. Static.

shadows.name: offset-action
shadows.purpose: Action edge. Revealed on hover under an edged pressable, held statically by an engaged writing field, and taken by an interactive card's shade on hover.

shadows.name: offset-action-hover
shadows.purpose: Grown action edge. Held while a trigger owns an open overlay — open mirrors hover, one step louder.

shadows.name: offset-action-danger
shadows.purpose: Danger edge. Replaces the action edge on an invalid field under focus.

shadows.name: menu-leading-rule
shadows.purpose: The inset accent rule on the currently navigated menu or select row. 2px marks engagement rather than proximity; Alert's role rule is the same 2px mark drawn as a left border.

shadows.name: shadow-size-by-theme
shadows.purpose: Offset size is a theme decision, not a component one. The same component feels differently pressed under a different palette.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Every state transition: box-shadow, translate, border-color, background-color. The whole motion vocabulary for controls.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: The single slower transition in the system: the determinate Progress indicator's scaleX. Nothing else uses it.

motion.name: navigation-progress
motion.purpose: A bar sweeping across the navigation progress track. Overlays have no entrance animation at all.

motion.name: skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: The loading placeholder breathes in ink, not light: bg-hover to bg-active and back. Opacity would dim the page showing through it.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: foundation.css collapses every animation, transition, and scroll behavior globally.

narrative.northStar: Ink & Instrument — a printed page you can press
narrative.overview:
Everything on screen is drawn, not lit. The references are the print shop and the machine shop: a well-set page, ruled forms, keys that travel when pressed. Corners are square, color is flat, borders are pen strokes, and shadows are offset marks with zero blur — the trace a raised object leaves on paper, not the glow of a light source. Nothing here emits light, because nothing printed does.

The identity is rationed by scale, and the rationing is the thesis: **a drawn edge means you can act on it.** *Instruments* — button, input, select trigger, checkbox, radio, switch, badge — keep the 1px pen, the accent edge on engage, and the grown edge while they hold an overlay open. *Surfaces* — card, alert, table wrapper, DataTable container — carry no resting stroke at all; they are read by their fill step (page → raised → overlay) plus the drawn grey shade. Overlays keep a frame because they float over arbitrary content. Where two strokes must meet, they share one seam rather than stacking. A border around a region only repeats what the surface already said, and repeating it at every nesting level is what made a dense screen unreadable.

The system runs on one pen and one vivid voice. The neutral ramp is a single ink used at full strength for text, strong borders, and solid fills, so a line and a fill always agree about what matters. Ink is never diluted, only rationed — and it is rationed by *pressure*, not by grey: ink (`border-strong`), hairline (`border` / `border-muted`), seam (`border-subtle`). Against that monochrome ground, exactly one chromatic voice — the accent — is reserved for what you can act on. Signals (danger, success, warning, info) carry meaning but never emphasis, so a screen full of status never becomes a screen full of shouting.

Depth is semantic before it is spatial. A grey offset shade means "this is a raised surface"; an accent edge means "this responds to you." Pressables are neutral at rest, reveal a thin accent edge on hover, and drop onto it under the press. Writing fields stay quiet until engaged and then cap off with a static edge that leaves when the pen lifts. Small controls are instruments: the chassis stays put while the inner key — a check, a thumb, a label — travels one pixel. Brutalism supplies the refusals (no gradients, no blur, no rounding, nothing that lies about structure) but not the aggression. The goal is precision, not rawness.

**Confirmed visual rejections.** This must not look like shadcn/ui (too soft, too rounded, too close to what everyone ships), Material Design (too corporate, too systematic), Stripe or Linear (lit rather than drawn — glow, gradients, blurred elevation; the precision is shared, the material is not), Bootstrap (no point of view), or a web-brutalism showcase (aggression as the point). What a person should feel using it is confidence and clarity, respect for the craft, and material distinction — made, not assembled from the same lit parts as everything else.
keyCharacteristics: Square by default — `0` radius everywhere except Radio's circle.
Surfaces carry no resting stroke; instruments keep the 1px pen.
One neutral ink at three pressures — ink, hairline, seam. No diluted grey.
One chromatic accent, reserved for interaction — never for decoration.
Offset shadows with zero blur; grey for surfaces, accent for engagement.
Flat fills only. No gradient, no blur, no opacity used as a styling device.
14px carries the interface; 12px carries labels. The floor is set by CJK.
Two-layer tokens: a theme writes 30 palette values, components read 69 semantic names and never touch a palette value directly.

rules.name: The One Ink, Three Pressures Rule
rules.body: The neutral ramp is a single ink, and a 1px stroke chooses how hard the pen is pressed: ink (`border-strong`) bounds a region that outranks the page, hairline (`border` / `border-muted`) bounds a control, seam (`border-subtle`) divides inside a surface. There is no fourth pressure and no "slightly softer black" between them. What this replaces is the old habit of drawing every seam at full hairline strength and then framing the group as well.

rules.name: The Border-Means-Act Rule
rules.body: A resting stroke is a claim that you can operate the thing it encloses. Instruments make that claim; surfaces do not. If a new region wants a border, the question is whether it is pressable — and if it is not, the answer is a fill step and a shade.

rules.name: The One Vivid Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent belongs solely to what you can act on. Hue carries meaning, never emphasis. If a mark is not focus, open ownership, hover intent, current selection, or a link, it does not get the accent.

rules.name: The Knockout Rule
rules.body: Every solid ships with its own foreground (`danger-solid` + `danger-fg-on-solid`). Never hand-pick a text color on a solid, and never mix roles — warning text on an info tint is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Palette-Swap Rule
rules.body: Components consume only the 69 semantic names (64 color + 5 shadow). A theme authors 30 palette values (`--surface-0…2`, `--tone-0…11`, `--signal-*`, `--signal-*-on`, `--shadow-size`, `--shadow-color`, `--shadow-color-overlay`) and nothing else; 28 of those are functional dependencies and `--tone-8` and `--tone-9` are the reserved ramp slots — `--tone-10` left reserve in this revision when `fg` moved onto it. Writing `--tone-4` or a raw hex inside a component is the one unforgivable color error: it breaks every theme at once. Dark mode is the same mechanism — a palette swap under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, not a separate set of component rules.

rules.name: The Two-Size Rule
rules.body: 14px carries the interface and 12px carries labels. Together they are 34 of the 36 explicit size utilities in the component sources — every one except Dialog's and Sheet's titles. Reaching past them is a claim that this element outranks the whole interface — Dialog and Sheet titles are the only components that earn it.

rules.name: The CJK-Floor Rule
rules.body: 12px is the minimum step for any script, and the floor is set by CJK, not by Latin taste. Hangul packs two or three jamo into one em and kanji can carry a dozen strokes, so both collapse below 12px where Latin at the same size still reads. The two interface steps therefore pin their own leading (`--text-xs--line-height: 1.45`, `--text-sm--line-height: 1.55`) rather than inheriting Tailwind's tighter defaults, which crowd CJK at 14px.

rules.name: The Per-Script Routing Rule
rules.body: Font fallback runs per codepoint, and a Korean face such as Apple SD Gothic Neo also covers the CJK ideograph block — so one flat family list cannot serve both Korean and Japanese: whichever is named first captures every ideograph and the other language renders in the wrong national glyph forms. `@layer base` therefore re-declares `font-family` per `:lang(ko)`, `:lang(ja)`, `:lang(zh)` and `:lang(zh-Hant)`. It is re-declared, not swapped through a variable, because preflight resolves `font-family` once on `html` and descendants inherit the already-resolved value. `:lang(ko)` additionally sets `word-break: keep-all` with `overflow-wrap: break-word` as the relief valve; Japanese and Chinese carry no inter-word spaces and must not inherit it. **The consuming application must set `lang` on the document** or none of this applies. `src/components/cjk.stories.tsx` is the rendered baseline — nothing else in the set contains a Hangul or Kana glyph, which is how a type scale that was unusable in Korean stayed green through 357 visual snapshots.

rules.name: The Weight-Before-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy inside a component is made with weight (400 → 500 → 600) and with ink color (`fg` → `fg-muted`), not by growing the type. A card title is the same size as its body text.

rules.name: The Fused Strip Rule
rules.body: Navigation, tab and pagination cells do not float as separate chips — they share one seam, and the strip carries no standing edge of its own. Two mechanisms are in use: Navigation borders the `<li>` and cancels the neighbour's leading border (`[&>li+li]:border-l-0`); Tabs and Pagination border the cell and pull it back one pixel (`-ml-px first:ml-0`). Either way the result is a single ruled line where two cells meet, never two. Gaps between cells break the instrument.

rules.name: The Drawn-Not-Lit Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is `<offset> <offset> 0 0 <color>`, and the offset is always down-and-right. Blur radius and spread are always zero. A blurred shadow claims a light source, and nothing on a printed page emits light. This also governs rims: ink gathers where the shade falls, so a two-tone rim is light on the top/left and ink on the bottom/right, never the reverse.

rules.name: The Shadow-Is-Voice Rule
rules.body: Grey shade = raised surface. Accent edge = engagement. A surface never takes the accent edge *at rest*; a passive surface never gains one at all. An interactive surface is the one crossing: it rests as a raised sheet with the grey shade and **changes voice** on hover — the same shade turns accent while the fill lifts one ladder step. Without a resting shade a borderless interactive card would be invisible until hovered.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one shadow utility may land in a class list. tailwind-merge cannot dedupe custom shadow utilities against one another, and `shadow-none` does not opt a variant out of `shadow-offset-action`. Assign the shade and the edge through mutually exclusive variants, never by layering and overriding.

rules.name: The Press-Drops-On Rule
rules.body: Pressing removes the shadow and translates the element one pixel toward it (`active:shadow-none active:translate-x-px active:translate-y-px`), so the control physically lands on the edge it revealed. Ghost and Link buttons opt out of both, because they never had an edge to drop onto.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Radius is `0`. The only circle in the system is Radio's chassis and its dot. If a new component wants a rounded corner, the answer is no — find the meaning that corner was carrying and draw it with a stroke.

rules.name: The No-Frame-On-Frame Rule
rules.body: Nothing draws a boundary that its container already drew. A table inside a card has no wrapper border; rows are parted by seams that reach the card's padding edge. An alert is a rule and a glyph on paper, not a box on a surface.

rules.name: The Dashed-Disabled Rule
rules.body: Disabled always means the same four things: dashed border, `border-muted` stroke, `bg-disabled` fill, `fg-disabled` text — plus removal of every shadow and interaction affordance. Never opacity.

rules.name: The Focus-Outermost Rule
rules.body: Keyboard focus always owns the outermost mark: a 2px accent outline offset 2px on pressables, the cap-off edge on writing fields. Open ownership, hover, and current-selection cues all stay inside it, so a focused control is unmistakable even in a row of selected and open ones. When a field is invalid, danger _replaces_ the accent in that indicator rather than layering over it.

rules.name: The One-Channel Rule
rules.body: Two cues never compete in the same visual channel. Open replaces the hover edge. Press drops the edge. Selection never borrows the focus outline. Disabled removes interaction edges and focus treatment entirely. Only spatially distinct channels may stack — most importantly, an outer focus outline around an open-owner edge or a selected fill.

rules.name: The Chassis Rule
rules.body: On an instrument, the chassis never moves. Only the inner key — a check, a dot, a thumb, a label — travels the 1px under a press.

dos: **Do** use only the 69 semantic token names (`bg-bg-raised`, `text-fg-muted`, `border-border-subtle`). They are the entire color and shadow API.
**Do** give a region a fill step and a shade instead of a border, unless it is an instrument you can operate.
**Do** pick the pressure that matches the job: `border-strong` for a region that outranks the page, `border` / `border-muted` for a control, and `border-subtle` for a divider inside a surface.
**Do** pair every role solid with its own knockout (`bg-danger-solid text-danger-fg-on-solid`), and every role tint with its full triple (`bg-{role}-bg` + `border-{role}-border` + `text-{role}-fg`).

**Do** give pressables the neutral rest / accent-edge-on-hover / grown-edge-while-open / drop-on-press sequence (`hover:shadow-offset-action data-[state=open]:shadow-offset-action-hover active:shadow-none active:translate-x-px active:translate-y-px`).

**Do** use one focus grammar on pressables — `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-border-focus focus-visible:outline-offset-2` — and cap-off on writing fields: `focus:outline-hidden not-read-only:focus:shadow-offset-action`.
**Do** use the one disabled pattern everywhere: `disabled:border-dashed disabled:border-border-muted disabled:bg-bg-disabled disabled:text-fg-disabled disabled:shadow-none`.

**Do** expand a standalone instrument to 44px (`before:absolute before:inset-[-15px] before:content-['']` on a 16px chassis), expand a fused cell vertically only (`before:inset-x-0 before:-inset-y-2` plus the strip's outer edges), and give stacked bare instruments a 44px pitch. Verify the measured box in a browser, not by arithmetic on the class name.

**Do** assign a variant's edge explicitly, and let exactly one shadow utility reach the class list. `shadow-none` does not opt a variant out of a custom `shadow-offset-action` — tailwind-merge cannot dedupe a custom shadow utility against it.
**Do** set `lang` on the document in the consuming app; the per-script font routing and Korean `keep-all` line breaking depend on it.
donts: **Don't** write a palette value (`--tone-4`, `--surface-1`, `--signal-accent`) or a raw color inside a component. Palette values belong to themes only.
**Don't** put a resting border on a surface, or a border on something already bounded by its container. A card inside a card, a table inside a card, and an alert on a page all draw zero frames.
**Don't** add a border radius. `rounded-lg`, `rounded-md`, and `rounded-sm` have no place here; Radio's `rounded-full` is the sole exception.

**Don't** use a blurred shadow (`shadow-md`, `shadow-lg`, any non-zero blur or spread), a gradient, or a backdrop blur — and don't reverse the offset direction or invert a two-tone rim; ink gathers down and to the right.
**Don't** use opacity as a styling device — not for disabled, not for muted text, not for hover, not for a loading placeholder. The modal scrim is the only alpha in the system.
**Don't** put a standing accent edge on an idle pressable, or an accent edge on a passive surface. Accent is a state, not a synonym for "interactive."
**Don't** let selection borrow the focus outline, or let hover and open cues stack in the same channel.
**Don't** give Ghost or Link buttons an edge or a press translation; they are not edged pressables.
**Don't** expand a fused cell horizontally — it steals clicks from its neighbour — and don't claim 44px for an `<input>`, which cannot carry a pseudo-element at all.
**Don't** reach past 14px/12px for component type, and don't go below 12px for any script. Use weight and ink color for hierarchy instead.
**Don't** put gaps between navigation, tab, or pagination cells — they fuse on a shared seam.
